memberdef.definition: void AGRemapCore::TemplateFixer::addFixSection
memberdef.name: addFixSection

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Adds a `section`_ the fix writes itself -- a resource it declares, a command list, a section on a draw the mod has none for -- to the ``.ini`` file the fix renders :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The sections go into the groups as ONE graph per group (see :cpp:class:`GraphCreate`), after every :cpp:member:`GIMIFixer::graphGroupEdits` entry has run and before :cpp:member:`fixSectionEdits`, so an edit run there reads and changes them as it does the mod's own. A section the group already renders with the same name and text is written once :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` :cpp:func:`giveUp` drops the sections added before it, and a section added AFTER it is still written, in a group of its own -- which is how a file that only watches the source carries its watching sections and nothing else

parameterdescription.para: The section
The one group it goes into. Default: the first group, and every copy too when :cpp:member:fixSectionsInCopies is set

memberdef.definition: TemplateFixer::GroupEdit * AGRemapCore::TemplateFixer::takeFixSections
memberdef.argsstring: (const ModObj &graph, std::vector< std::string > sections, const std::string &comment="", bool inPlace=false)
memberdef.name: takeFixSections

para.verbatim:
embed:rst An edit for :cpp:member:`GIMIFixer::graphGroupEdits` that makes `sections`_ an earlier edit built in a graph into the fix's own: each named `section`_ of graph 'graph' goes to :cpp:func:`addFixSection`, and the graph is removed :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` This is how a fix section is built from the mod's own sections by edits: copy them into a graph of their own (:cpp:class:`GraphCopy`), edit that graph, then take the result. The edit is owned by this fixer :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The sections taken are written after every section :cpp:func:`addFixSection` added before the edit runs -- or, with 'inPlace', where this call stands among them: after the sections added before it and before the ones added after it

parameterdescription.para: The graph, in the first group
The sections_ to take, in order. A name the graph does not hold is skipped
A comment written above each section taken. Default: none
Whether the sections keep this call's place among the fix's sections. Default: false

memberdef.definition: std::string AGRemapCore::GIMIFixer< std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>, BaseIniFixer<std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>> >::copyPreamble
memberdef.name: copyPreamble

para.verbatim:
embed:rst What every generated ``.ini`` **copy** is prefixed with :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A fix that merges several mod objects onto one emits an extra ``.ini`` file per extra object (see :cpp:func:`IniFileFixContext::fixedFilePath` for how they are named). Each of those is a file the user never asked for and did not write, so each one opens by saying what it is :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Only the **copies** get it. Group 0 is the mod's own ``.ini`` file, which needs no explanation of why it exists :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: empty -- no preamble at all. A generated file that says nothing about itself is the quieter default, and a caller that wants the explanation opts in. :cpp:member:`IniComments::GIMIObjMergerPreamble` is the one written for this purpose

memberdef.definition: std::string AGRemapCore::GIMIFixer< std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>, BaseIniFixer<std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>> >::appendedSections
memberdef.name: appendedSections

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Raw `sections`_ appended to the mod's OWN ``.ini`` file, after everything else :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` For content that belongs to the fix as a whole rather than to any object it copies, and so has no source section to be edited from. The one use so far is suppressing the draw of a TARGET component nothing was remapped onto: such a component still draws the skin's own geometry, on top of whatever the mod put there, and the only way to stop it is a ``TextureOverride`` on its ib hash with ``handling = skip`` and no draw. Group 0 and not the copies, deliberately -- it is written once per ``.ini`` file the fix touches, where a copy is written once per generated file. A caller producing several fixers over one ``.ini`` must therefore pick ONE of them to carry this, or the same section name lands in the file twice **Default**: empty

memberdef.definition: bool AGRemapCore::GIMIFixer< std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>, BaseIniFixer<std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>> >::appendedSectionsInCopies
memberdef.name: appendedSectionsInCopies

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Whether :cpp:member:`appendedSections` goes into every generated COPY as well as the mod's own ``.ini`` file :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A copy's sections reference the fix's own command lists and resources by name; a GIMI merge is fine with those living in the mod's own file alone, but a WWMI copy is not -- unless its copies carry the texture command lists and resources themselves, every body part is drawn with the FIRST claimant's textures. **Default**: ``false``

memberdef.definition: std::map<std::size_t, std::string> AGRemapCore::GIMIFixer< std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>, BaseIniFixer<std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>> >::appendedSectionsPerGroup
memberdef.name: appendedSectionsPerGroup

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Raw `sections`_ appended to ONE generated file only, by group -- ``0`` is the mod's own ``.ini``, ``1`` its first copy, and so on. Written after :cpp:member:`appendedSections`, inside the fix's block :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` For content that differs per file: a WWMI copy keeps its own merged skeleton, which only the draws that FILE matches feed, so each copy needs merge-only sections for the target slots that other files draw. **Default**: empty

memberdef.definition: bool AGRemapCore::GIMIFixer< std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>, BaseIniFixer<std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>> >::appendedSectionsDropRepeats
memberdef.name: appendedSectionsDropRepeats

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Whether an appended section (:cpp:member:`appendedSections`, :cpp:member:`appendedSectionsPerGroup`) that the file already declares WORD FOR WORD is left out :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` 3DMigoto keeps the first of two sections with one name and warns about the second, so a repeat changes nothing but the warning. A same-named section with different text is kept, so a real conflict still shows. **Default**: ``false``

memberdef.definition: std::unordered_set<std::string> AGRemapCore::GIMIFixer< std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>, BaseIniFixer<std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>> >::copyHiddenSectionNames
memberdef.name: copyHiddenSectionNames

para.verbatim:
embed:rst The mod's own sections commented out in every generated COPY, and left alone in the mod's own file -- in addition to whatever #hiddenModObjs and ``hideOrig`` hide everywhere :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The WWMI fixer names every ``TextureOverride`` of the mod's own text here: the mod's own file keeps serving the mod on its source character, and a copy exists only to carry one more remapped section onto a draw the first file already claimed. **Default**: empty

memberdef.definition: std::unordered_set<ModObj, ModObjHash> AGRemapCore::GIMIFixer< std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>, BaseIniFixer<std::string, std::string, std::hash<std::string>, std::equal_to<std::string>> >::hiddenModObjs
memberdef.name: hiddenModObjs

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Mod objects whose **original** `sections`_ are commented out of the source text this fix appends :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Every fix that runs with ``withSrc`` opens with the ``.ini`` file's own content, so the original mod keeps working alongside the remap. That is usually what you want, but not always: when the fix *replaces* what a mod object drew rather than adding beside it, leaving the original in means the game draws both. Naming that mod object here comments its `sections`_ out with :cpp:member:`IniKeywords::HideOriginalComment`, so the appended source still explains what was there without it still being live :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Raiden's 6.1 fix is the case this exists for: it rewrites ``head``/``body``/``dress`` in place, so the original three have to go :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: This is **independent of the ``hideOrig`` flag** #fixImpl is handed. That flag is the *user's* "hide the original mod entirely" request and hides everything #touchedSectionNames covers; this is the *fixer's* own "these particular objects cannot survive my fix", and applies whether or not the user asked for anything. When both are in play the two sets are hidden together .. note:: Unlike #touchedSectionNames, nothing is filtered out of this set -- no :cpp:member:`IniGraphModObjKeywords::Download` check, no :cpp:member:`IniKeywords::Remap` check. Those exist to stop an *inferred* set from hiding something it shouldn't; this set is written out by hand, so it is taken at its word **Default**: empty -- hide nothing beyond what ``hideOrig`` asks for

memberdef.name: prevFixer

para.verbatim:
embed:rst A fixer whose already-edited groups this one continues from -- borrowed, ``nullptr`` for none :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` When set, #getFix runs *that* fixer's edit pass first and takes over its groups outright (a pointer move, not a copy), leaving it empty

embed:rst The base of a plain-C++ fixer that fixes one :cpp:class:`AGRemapCore::IniFile` by a list of edits :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A subclass builds its edits in its constructor and puts them, in the order they run, in :cpp:member:`GIMIFixer::graphGroupEdits`. The sections it writes of its own (sections that belong to no mod object) are built as `section`_\ s with :cpp:func:`makeSection` or :cpp:func:`renderSection` and handed over through :cpp:member:`GIMIFixer::appendedSections`. This class then supplies what every such fixer needs and none of them is about: * the fix context: an :cpp:class:`IniFileFixContext` over the parser's ``.ini`` file, owned here and installed as the fixer's context * the section renderer: :cpp:func:`renderIfTemplate` * applying the edits: :cpp:func:`applyGraphGroupEdits` hands every edit the REAL ``.ini`` file, so a :cpp:class:`ResRegCollect` can build the resources it collects (the :cpp:class:`GIMIFixer` default hands them ``nullptr``) * giving up: :cpp:func:`giveUp` replaces the edit list with one :cpp:class:`GraphGroupRemove`, so the fixer writes nothing for the ``.ini`` file rather than the mod's own sections again under their source names :raw-html:`
` .. note:: `C++`_ only. A fixer built from `Python`_ gets the same behaviour from the bound :cpp:class:`GIMIFixer`, whose `pybind11`_ layer already hands its edits the real `Python`_ ``IniFile``, so there is nothing of this class for such a fixer to reach
